openQuestions: Population boundary. 'Frontier model release' was read as a general-purpose generative language or multimodal-language model of the developers' model families (Meta: LLaMA/Llama, Code Llama, Muse; Microsoft: Phi, MAI), plus Meta's CWM because Meta assessed it under its framework. Located but treated as outside: safeguard classifiers (Llama Guard 1-4, Prompt Guard 1-2), GUI-grounding models (Phi-Ground, Phi-Ground-Any) and compression-research checkpoints (Phi-mini-MoE, Phi-tiny-MoE); not inventoried: Meta FAIR on-device research models (MobileLLM, MobileMoE) and Microsoft research models outside Phi and MAI (Orca 2, BitNet, Magma, UserLM, Fara). Including them would change three rows under the mechanical rule: Meta 2023 would be Llama Guard (December 2023) instead of Llama 2, Meta 2025 would be MobileLLM-R1.5 (Hugging Face, November 2025) instead of the CWM report, and Microsoft 2025 would be Phi-Ground (September 2025) instead of Phi-4-mini-flash-reasoning. Recommendation: keep the boundary and state it in scope.md.

Which date orders cards. Following the brief, ambiguous dates were resolved by the card's own printed date. Meta 2026 is therefore the Muse Spark 1.3 Evaluation Report, which prints 'Date: October 23, 2026' but was linked from Meta's announcement of September 2, 2026; under an earliest-publication reading the Muse Spark Open model card (published 2026-10-15; cached as meta-muse-spark-open, not drafted) would be the 2026 row. For 2025 the CWM report (printed October 8, 2025) and the CWM model card share the publication date September 24, 2025, so the printed date decides either way. Recommendation: decide whether revision dates may reorder cards and record the reading in scope.md; if not, swap the 2026 Meta row.
